title: The iPhone, Android, and the 2008 Birth of the App Store Model
explainer: The idea of a single marketplace for installing third-party mobile software is barely two decades old. Apple's App Store launched in July 2008, and Google's Android Market (now Google Play) followed that October alongside the HTC Dream/T-Mobile G1, the first commercially released Android phone. Cross-platform mobile frameworks exist precisely because these two ecosystems grew up with separate languages, toolchains, and store requirements instead of a shared standard.

title: PhoneGap and the 2008 Start of 'Write Once, Run on Any Phone'
explainer: Long before React Native or Flutter, a small Vancouver company called Nitobi built PhoneGap in 2008 to let web developers wrap HTML, CSS, and JavaScript inside a native app shell. Adobe acquired Nitobi in 2011 and donated the code to the Apache Software Foundation, where it lives on today as Apache Cordova. Today's cross-platform frameworks are solving the same cross-OS problem PhoneGap first tackled, just with native UI components instead of an embedded web view.
